p0.original: This division of labour, from which so many advantages are derived, is not originally the effect of any human wisdom, which foresees and intends that general opulence to which it gives occasion. It is the necessary, though very slow and gradual, consequence of a certain propensity in human nature, which has in view no such extensive utility; the propensity to truck, barter, and exchange one thing for another.
p0.zh: 这种分工产生许多好处,最初并不是任何人类智慧的效果,这种智慧预见并意图产生它所赋予的普遍财富。 这是人性中某种倾向所必须的,尽管非常缓慢和渐进,但这种倾向并没有如此广泛的作用;它倾向于卡车、易货和将一种东西换成另一种东西。

p1.original: Whether this propensity be one of those original principles in human nature, of which no further account can be given, or whether, as seems more probable, it be the necessary consequence of the faculties of reason and speech, it belongs not to our present subject to inquire. It is common to all men, and to be found in no other race of animals, which seem to know neither this nor any other species of contracts. Two greyhounds, in running down the same hare, have sometimes the appearance of acting in some sort of concert. Each turns her towards his companion, or endeavours to intercept her when his companion turns her towards himself. This, however, is not the effect of any contract, but of the accidental concurrence of their passions in the same object at that particular time. Nobody ever saw a dog make a fair and deliberate exchange of one bone for another with another dog. Nobody ever saw one animal, by its gestures and natural cries signify to another, this is mine, that yours; I am willing to give this for that. When an animal wants to obtain something either of a man, or of another animal, it has no other means of persuasion, but to gain the favour of those whose service it requires. A puppy fawns upon its dam, and a spaniel endeavours, by a thousand attractions, to engage the attention of its master who is at dinner, when it wants to be fed by him. Man sometimes uses the same arts with his brethren, and when he has no other means of engaging them to act according to his inclinations, endeavours by every servile and fawning attention to obtain their good will. He has not time, however, to do this upon every occasion. In civilized society he stands at all times in need of the co-operation and assistance of great multitudes, while his whole life is scarce sufficient to gain the friendship of a few persons. In almost every other race of animals, each individual, when it is grown up to maturity, is entirely independent, and in its natural state has occasion for the assistance of no other living creature. But man has almost constant occasion for the help of his brethren, and it is in vain for him to expect it from their benevolence only. He will be more likely to prevail if he can interest their self-love in his favour, and shew them that it is for their own advantage to do for him what he requires of them. Whoever offers to another a bargain of any kind, proposes to do this. Give me that which I want, and you shall have this which you want, is the meaning of every such offer; and it is in this manner that we obtain from one another the far greater part of those good offices which we stand in need of. It is not from the benevolence of the butcher, the brewer, or the baker that we expect our dinner, but from their regard to their own interest. We address ourselves, not to their humanity, but to their self-love, and never talk to them of our own necessities, but of their advantages. Nobody but a beggar chooses to depend chiefly upon the benevolence of his fellow-citizens. Even a beggar does not depend upon it entirely. The charity of well-disposed people, indeed, supplies him with the whole fund of his subsistence. But though this principle ultimately provides him with all the necessaries of life which he has occasion for, it neither does nor can provide him with them as he has occasion for them. The greater part of his occasional wants are supplied in the same manner as those of other people, by treaty, by barter, and by purchase. With the money which one man gives him he purchases food. The old clothes which another bestows upon him he exchanges for other clothes which suit him better, or for lodging, or for food, or for money, with which he can buy either food, clothes, or lodging, as he has occasion.
p1.zh: 不论这种倾向是人类性质的原始原则之一,不能进一步加以说明,还是似乎更有可能是理性和言论能力的必要后果,它不属于我们目前要调查的对象。 它在所有人中都是常见的,并且没有其他的动物种族,这些动物似乎既不了解这个种类,也不了解任何其他种类的契约. 两只灰狗在跑下同一只兔子时,有时会出现某种音乐会中的表演. 他们都把她转向他的伙伴,或想在伙伴使她转向自己的时候拦截她。 然而,这并不是任何契约的效果,而是他们当时在同一个对象上偶然同意的激情的效果.从来没有人见过一只狗 公平而故意地把骨头换成另一只狗 没有人见过一只动物,通过它的姿态和自然的呼喊,代表着另一只动物,这是我的,我愿意为此付出。 当动物想要获得某种东西 无论是男人还是其他动物, 它没有其他的说服手段, 只能得到服务的人的青睐。一只小狗在大坝上 一只小狗在一千个景点下 努力吸引着它主人的注意 当它想被他喂饱的时候人有时与兄弟们使用同样的艺术,当他没有其他手段让他们按照他的倾向行事时,每个侍从和放荡的注意力都为获得他们的善意而努力。 然而,他没有时间每次都这样做。 在文明社会中,他随时需要广大人民的合作和援助,而他的一生却不足以获得少数人的友谊。几乎在所有其他的动物种族中,每个个体在成熟到成熟时都是完全独立的,在其自然状态下,没有其他生物有帮助的机会.人几乎常求兄弟的帮助,他只希望他们的慈恩是徒劳的。 如果他能为他的利益而关心他们的自我爱,并让他们知道,为了他们自己的利益,为他做他要求他们做的事,他就会更可能获胜.任何人向另一个人提出任何交易,都提议这样做。给予我我想要的,你们将得到的,是每一个这种提议的意义;我们正是以这种方式从彼此之间获得我们所需要的斡旋的更大部分。 我们期待的不是屠夫、酿酒师或面包师的仁慈,而是他们关心自己的利益。 我们不是针对他们的人性,而是针对他们的自我爱,从不与他们谈论我们自己的需要,而是谈论他们的优势。 只有乞丐才会选择主要依靠同胞的慈悲。连乞丐也不完全依赖它。善于施舍的民众,的确为他提供了他赖以生存的全部资金。 但是,虽然这一原则最终为他提供了他所寻求的一切生活必需品,但是,它既不能,也不能象他所希望的那样,为他提供这些必需品。 他偶尔想要的,大部分都以和其他人一样的方式提供,通过条约,通过易货,通过购买.一个人给他的钱 他买食物。别人给他的旧衣服,他用其他衣服换来更适合他的衣服,或用来住宿,或用来吃饭,或用来换钱,他可以用这些衣服购买食物、衣服或住宿,就像他所见过的。

p2.original: As it is by treaty, by barter, and by purchase, that we obtain from one another the greater part of those mutual good offices which we stand in need of, so it is this same trucking disposition which originally gives occasion to the division of labour. In a tribe of hunters or shepherds, a particular person makes bows and arrows, for example, with more readiness and dexterity than any other. He frequently exchanges them for cattle or for venison, with his companions; and he finds at last that he can, in this manner, get more cattle and venison, than if he himself went to the field to catch them. From a regard to his own interest, therefore, the making of bows and arrows grows to be his chief business, and he becomes a sort of armourer. Another excels in making the frames and covers of their little huts or moveable houses. He is accustomed to be of use in this way to his neighbours, who reward him in the same manner with cattle and with venison, till at last he finds it his interest to dedicate himself entirely to this employment, and to become a sort of house-carpenter. In the same manner a third becomes a smith or a brazier; a fourth, a tanner or dresser of hides or skins, the principal part of the clothing of savages. And thus the certainty of being able to exchange all that surplus part of the produce of his own labour, which is over and above his own consumption, for such parts of the produce of other men's labour as he may have occasion for, encourages every man to apply himself to a particular occupation, and to cultivate and bring to perfection whatever talent of genius he may possess for that particular species of business.
p2.zh: 正如我们通过条约、以易货和购买,从彼此那里获得我们目前需要的更多相互斡旋,因此,正是这种同样的卡车处置方式才最初为分工提供了机会。 在猎人或牧羊人的部落中,特定的人会制作弓箭,例如比其他任何的人都更准备和狡猾. 他经常与同伴用牛换牛,或换食肉动物;他终于发现,他能够以这种方式获得更多的牛和食肉动物,比他自己去田野捕捉牛还要多. 因此,从他自身的利益出发,弓箭的制作逐渐成长为他的首席业务,他也成为了某种装甲兵.另一家公司在制作小屋或可移动房屋的架子和盖子方面表现优异。 他习惯于用这种方式对待邻居们,邻居们以同样的方式用牛和食肉来奖励他,直到他终于发现他的兴趣是完全致力于这种工作,并成为某种家庭木匠。以同样的方式,第三者成为铁匠或胸围;第四者成为皮毛或皮革的制革者或梳妆者,是野蛮人服装的主要部分. 因此,能够将自己劳动中超出自己消费的剩余部分的剩余部分换取其他男子劳动中他有机会从事的这些部分的确定性,鼓励每个人投身于某一特定职业,培养和完善他为这一特定行业可能拥有的天才人才。

p3.original: The difference of natural talents in different men, is, in reality, much less than we are aware of; and the very different genius which appears to distinguish men of different professions, when grown up to maturity, is not upon many occasions so much the cause, as the effect of the division of labour. The difference between the most dissimilar characters, between a philosopher and a common street porter, for example, seems to arise not so much from nature, as from habit, custom, and education. When they came in to the world, and for the first six or eight years of their existence, they were, perhaps, very much alike, and neither their parents nor play-fellows could perceive any remarkable difference. About that age, or soon after, they come to be employed in very different occupations. The difference of talents comes then to be taken notice of, and widens by degrees, till at last the vanity of the philosopher is willing to acknowledge scarce any resemblance. But without the disposition to truck, barter, and exchange, every man must have procured to himself every necessary and conveniency of life which he wanted. All must have had the same duties to perform, and the same work to do, and there could have been no such difference of employment as could alone give occasion to any great difference of talents.
p3.zh: 不同男人的天赋差异,在现实中,远不如我们所意识到的;而那些似乎区别不同职业的男子,在成熟时,在很多时候,其原因并不太多,而是劳动分工的效果。哲学家和普通的街头搬运工之间最不相似的人物之间的区别,似乎不是源于自然,而是源于习惯、习俗和教育。 当他们来到世界, 在他们存在的头六八年里, 他们也许非常相似, 他们的父母和玩耍的主人都看不出任何显著的区别。大约在那个年龄,或不久之后,她们就受雇于非常不同的职业。才智的差别会逐渐被人们注意到, 并随着程度而扩大, 直到哲学家的虚荣终于愿意承认 几乎没有任何相似之处。 但是,如果没有对卡车、易货和交换的处置,每个人都必须为自己购买他想要的一切生活所必需的和允许性。所有人都必须承担同样的职责,必须从事同样的工作,就业方面的差别不可能单独产生任何巨大的人才差异。

p4.original: As it is this disposition which forms that difference of talents, so remarkable among men of different professions, so it is this same disposition which renders that difference useful. Many tribes of animals, acknowledged to be all of the same species, derive from nature a much more remarkable distinction of genius, than what, antecedent to custom and education, appears to take place among men. By nature a philosopher is not in genius and disposition half so different from a street porter, as a mastiff is from a grey-hound, or a grey-hound from a spaniel, or this last from a shepherd's dog. Those different tribes of animals, however, though all of the same species are of scarce any use to one another. The strength of the mastiff is not in the least supported either by the swiftness of the greyhound, or by the sagacity of the spaniel, or by the docility of the shepherd's dog. The effects of those different geniuses and talents, for want of the power or disposition to barter and exchange, cannot be brought into a common stock, and do not in the least contribute to the better accommodation and conveniency of the species. Each animal is still obliged to support and defend itself, separately and independently, and derives no sort of advantage from that variety of talents with which nature has distinguished its fellows. Among men, on the contrary, the most dissimilar geniuses are of use to one another; the different produces of their respective talents, by the general disposition to truck, barter, and exchange, being brought, as it were, into a common stock, where every man may purchase whatever part of the produce of other men's talents he has occasion for.
